source_refs.note: Chapter 3 summary (PDF 46), with its definitions arranged as a table.

blocks.text: This chapter showed how Python programs can be built from classes and objects, and how encapsulation, inheritance and polymorphism make them safer, reusable and flexible. The table brings together its main terms.

blocks.caption: Chapter 3 key terms
rows: Designing a program using objects that represent real-world entities
A blueprint or template for objects that defines their properties and behaviours
An instance of a class: a real-world entity with its own data and functions
Dividing a program into smaller parts that can be developed and maintained separately
Using already written code again in other parts of a program or in other programs
Keeping data and its methods together in a class and protecting the data from unauthorised access
One class using the properties and methods of another class
The same method or operation working differently depending on the object
